Judgment

This appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (the Act) has been filed by the claim petitioner in O.P.(MV) No.2094/2012 on the file of the Additional Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Thrissur, (the Tribunal), aggrieved by the amount of compensation granted by Award dated 21/05/2019.

sentences.text: The respondents herein are the respondents in the petition.
In this appeal, the parties and the documents will be referred to as described in the original petition.

2. According to the claim petitioner, on 04/09/2011 at about 09:30 p.m., while he was riding his motorcycle bearing registration No.KL-08/AU-9313 through Perumbillissery- Poochinnipadam public road and when he reached near Murali Tile 2025:KER:50005 Factory, Poochinnipadam, car bearing registration No.KL-08/AL- 4048 driven by the second respondent in a rash and negligent manner knocked him down as a result of which he sustained grievous injuries.
An amount of 33,00,415/- was claimed as compensation under various heads.

3. The first respondent/owner and the second respondent/driver remained ex parte.
4.
The third respondent/insurer filed written statement admitting the policy, but denying negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver.
It was also contended that the amount claimed was excessive.

2 5.
Before the Tribunal, PW1 sand PW2 were examined and Exts.A1 to A19 were marked on the side of the claim petitioner.
No oral or documentary evidence was adduced by the respondents.

6. The Tribunal on consideration of the oral and documentary evidence and after hearing both sides,
found negligence on the part of the second respondent/driver of the 2025:KER:50005 offending vehicle resulting in the incident and hence awarded an amount of 8,12,746/- together with interest @ 9% per annum from the date of the petition till the date of realisation with proportionate costs.
Aggrieved by the Award, the claim petitioner has come up in appeal.
7. The only point that arises for consideration in this appeal is whether there is any infirmity in the findings of the Tribunal calling for an interference by this Court.
8. Heard both sides.
9. The award of compensation by the Tribunal under the following heads is challenged by the claim petitioner - Contributory negligence

It is submitted by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner that the Tribunal after having found that the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle was rash and negligent, erred in concluding that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claim petitioner and deducting 50% out of the amount awarded.

In support of the argument, he relies on the dictums in Sudhir Kumar Rana v.
2025:KER:50005 Surinder Singh, (2008) 12 SCC 436 and Mohammed Noufal T. v. Saheed, 2018 (1)
KHC 507.

sentences.text: Per contra, it is submitted by the learned Senior Counsel appearing for the third respondent/insurer that the fact that the claim petitioner did not have a valid driving license at the relevant time itself would show that he was negligent and therefore, the Tribunal was justified in finding contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and reducing 50% of the award amount.
Hence, there is no infirmity calling for an interference by this court, goes the argument.

9.1. As rightly pointed out by the learned counsel for the claim petitioner, in paragraph no.8 of the impugned Award, the Tribunal has concluded that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the second respondent/ driver of the offending vehicle.
However, in paragraph no.17, the Tribunal went on to hold that there was 50% contributory negligence on the part of the claimant as he failed to produce his driving license.
Therefore, the Tribunal went on to fix 50% as contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and thereby reduced 50% of the amount awarded.
It is well settled that 2025:KER:50005 mere absence of driving license is not a ground to hold that the driver was rash or negligent.

As held by the Apex Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana (Supra) if a person drives a vehicle without a license, he commits an offence and the same by itself would not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident.

When Ext.A15 final report filed in the crime shows that it was the second respondent/driver of the offending vehicle who was negligent, the Tribunal could not have in the absence of any other materials or evidence held that there was contributory negligence.
No evidence has been let in to disprove the final report.
That being so, the finding of the Tribunal that there was contributory negligence on the part of the claim petitioner is wrong and so liable to be interfered with and hence I do so.

However, the same has not been granted by the Tribunal, 2025:KER:50005 an error committed by the Tribunal which needs to be rectified by this Court, argues the counsel.

11. The Tribunal accepted the certificate and assessed his functional disability also at 49.4%, which disability is quite high.
When the disability has been fixed as 49.4%, he would be entitled to compensation towards loss of future prospects.
The claim petitioner was aged 25 years at the time of the incident and therefore, the addition to be made to the income is 40%.
